/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 45

Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$,
such that every integer $\leq N$ lies in at least 10 of them?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
- [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)

The version of this problem with $10$ replaced by $2$ is `Erdos689.erdos_689` in
`FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»`.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Green45

/--
Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$, such that every
integer $\leq N$ lies in at least $10$ of them?

Erdős remarks that he does not know how to answer it with $10$ replaced by $2$;
this is `Erdos689.erdos_689`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_45 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ N in .atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      10 ≤ (Finset.Icc 1 N |>.filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card := by
  sorry

end Green45

sources_consulted: Ben Green, 100 Open Problems, December 2025 update: notation on p. 2 and Problem 45 with comments on p. 23. https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45
Paul Erdős, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory, Annals of Discrete Mathematics 6 (1980), 89–115, §6, especially Problem 6 on p. 108. https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf
Erdős collected-papers archive and bibliographic index, entry 1980-03: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, Green45.green_45. Its quantifier order, positive interval [1,N], prime bound p ≤ N, and coverage multiplicity ≥ 10 faithfully express Green's question. Erdős's original survey supports the sufficiently-large-parameter interpretation. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved equivalence with an explicit threshold and canonical representatives 0 ≤ a_p < p, and verified small-input behavior, including impossibility for 1 ≤ N ≤ 28. These proofs do not depend on sorry axioms. The cited erdosproblems.com/689 page could not be read because Cloudflare blocked requests despite descriptive User-Agent headers; its latest status therefore remains unchecked. The accessible Green PDF still presents the problem as open.
